index_line: - [[elac-carina-bs243-4]] — 6 Ω, AMT tweeter, LW ±2.8 dB, f3 54 Hz, sens 82.2 dB, min 4.6 Ω, pref 4.9 (ASR)
source_index_lines: - [[mfr-elac-carina-bs243-4]] — Elac/World Wide Stereo specs and price (Tier C)
brand_notes: Carina series sits between Debut and Adante/Vela; designed by Andrew Jones, first Elac with AMT (JET) tweeter in the US line; downward-firing port on metal plinth. Elac US site lists Carina as current while Adante AS-61, BS 41 and BS 314 are not on elac.com (see their sidecars). Measured sensitivity ~2.5-3 dB below the 85 dB claim; claimed 4.8 ohm min measured 4.6 (asr-, stereophile-elac-carina-bs243-4).
takeaways: Klippel: LW ±2.8 dB, smooth DI, very wide 153 deg horizontal beamwidth; dip near 2.8 kHz is the main flaw (ASR).
Sensitivity measured 82.2 dB (ASR) / ~82.5 dB (Stereophile) vs 85 dB claimed.
Min impedance 4.6 Ω by both ASR and Stereophile: below-iec for 6 Ω nominal.
Critics (Stereophile, TAS) praise refinement and bass weight; both note placement sensitivity.
ASR THD: ~2.3% at 86 dB near 100 Hz and a resonance near 1.9 kHz; no compression test.
conflicts: Min impedance claimed 4.8 vs measured 4.6 Ω
Dimensions on maker page ambiguous vs Stereophile
